title: Measures to Prevent Radicalisation of At-risk Youths
what_it_is: Measures to Prevent Radicalisation of At-risk Youths

sections.label: Community efforts against radicalisation
sections.summary: The Government works with community groups, IRCCs, religious and youth leaders, and Self Help Groups to raise awareness of radicalisation, while the Muslim community counters jihadi ideology.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The Government has been working with various community groups and organisations to deal with this issue.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Among other things, we work with the Inter-Racial and Religious Harmony Circles (IRCCs).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: MCCY has been engaging the leaders of religious organisations as well as youth leaders in the community and our Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The approach and purpose are to sensitise them to the threat of radicalisation and the need to be vigilant.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: We will continue to work with community organisations, Self Help Groups (SHGs) like CDAC, Mendaki, the Eurasian Association and SINDA, to increase the awareness of this issue amongst our youths.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Our local Muslim community and religious organisations have also put in considerable effort to counter the radical ideology of the jihadi terrorist groups like ISIS.

sections.label: Foreign preachers entry restriction
sections.summary: Foreign religious preachers whose teachings are intolerant of other faiths and practices are not allowed to come to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: One example is the fact that we do not allow foreign religious preachers to come to Singapore if their teachings are intolerant of other religious faiths and practices.

sections.label: Religious freedom and security risk
sections.summary: Freedom of religion is guaranteed by the Constitution, but religious groups promoting actions contrary to social harmony or threatening safety will be treated as a security risk.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Freedom of religion is guaranteed under our Constitution.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: But any religious group, whether registered or informal, that preaches values or promotes actions that are directly contrary to our social harmony and cohesion, or threaten our safety and security, will be treated as a security risk.

sections.label: Denial based on teachings
sections.summary: A person's teachings, said in or outside Singapore, will be examined and denied if contrary to our values.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: What are his teachings, what has he said whether in Singapore or outside of Singapore, and, if his teachings are contrary to our values, he will be denied.
